SMGT 430.d: This course covers a few classes of statistical models that get used extensively in the profession of sport analytics, divided into three units: Measuring Team Strength, Estimating Player Talent, and Valuing Event Outcomes. For each model, we discuss its mathematical underpinnings and how to interpret the results, bridging the gap from model land to real life. We implement all models in R using current real-world data from a wide variety of sports, and students complete assignments to practice generalizing concepts to other sports. A final project encourages students to dive deeply into a model they've learned in our outside of class by applying it to a problem about which they are passionate. Topics include the Bradley-Terry model, regression to the mean, mixed-effects models, Regularized Adjusted Plus-Minus, Markov chains, and Markov decision processes. Graduate/Undergraduate Equivalency: SMGT 530. Mutually Exclusive: Cannot register for SMGT 430 if student has credit for SMGT 530.
SMGT 430.pre: SMGT 330 and (STAT 310 or STAT 315 or DSCI 301 or ECON 307)
SMGT 430.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

Students will learn how to construct an effective resume, interview skills, business etiquette, etc. Students will also gain real-life experience by working with one of the numerous sports organizations in Houston for 100 hours during the course of the semester.
SMGT 276.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

SMGT 365.d: This course introduces the core principles of mediation. Within the class each student will become familiar with the nature of conflict, have a better understanding of culture awareness, as well as the ethics within the field of mediation. Students will conduct a full mediation while maintaining neutrality, exhibiting negotiation skills, and drafting agreements.

SMGT 467.d: Successful journalists must be able to communicate through their writing, their spoken word, and also through video. Students in this class will learn all of the different journalism formats and techniques including writing short and long articles, blogging, videos, podcasts, interviews, PR writing, social media, etc. Students will complete assignments in each of these areas. When students finish the course, they will have an updated portfolio filled with examples of their work. Recommended Prerequisite(s): SMGT 466

Students will engage in traditional classroom learning while also tackling real-world problems and creating potential solutions. Each week a different operating area will be examined.

The lab focuses on the use of software to analyze data from research in sport management. Students who enroll in this lab section must also enroll in SOSC 302 during the same semester.

It will provide the most current information available for training elite athletes in the area of strength, power, speed, and flexibility. Experts in the field of strength training, plyometrics, speed training, and flexibility will speak. The nature and basis of elite athlete training related to exercise physiology, biomechanics, motor learning, sport psychology, and nutrition will be explored.
SMGT 415.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

SMGT 440.d: In this age of Big Data, employees must be tech savvy with a strong background in computer and statistical analysis. Sport Business Analytics calls for special approaches to marketing and pricing. This course is designed to introduce the students to techniques that will allow for productive sport business analytics.
SMGT 440.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

SMGT 368.d: This course is designed to provide the student a deeper understanding of the way sport shapes the identity of people across diverse social groups such as race, ethnicity, class, gender, sexual orientation, age and (dis)ability. A historical perspective combined with critical analysis of modern issues will enable the student to explore sport as a microcosm of society
SMGT 368.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

SMGT 266.d: This course will examine industry leaders in customer service, identifying the unique qualities that their employees exhibit. Students will learn the fundamentals of service delivery and various research and various research and analysis methods, then apply those in practical applications with local sports franchises. By the conclusion of this course, students will have created a customer service vision for a fictitious organization, developed training programs for employees and created measurable objectives for success.
SMGT 266.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

Students will analyze sport cases and materials that cover multiple disciplines, including contracts, torts, constitutional law, labor and employment, and criminal law. Students will augment their learning through analysis and discussion of up-to-the-minute professional and collegiate sports law developments.
SMGT 464.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

Students will be expected to evaluate and understand the nuances that go into event and venue management with the help of assignments, case studies, guest speakers and practical experience (when possible). At conclusion of this course a student should fully understand what goes into creating and managing a successful event.

Students will learn to collect, manage, analyze, visualize, and interpret sports-related data to support decision-making in areas such as fan engagement, ticket sales, operations, marketing, and business strategy. Emphasis is placed on practical, hands-on experience with industry-relevant tools, ethical considerations, and storytelling with data.
SMGT 340.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

SMGT 390.d: This course will focus on the dynamic field of global sport management. Special emphasis will be given to the business functions, strategies and challenges of the international sport world. Students will examine such topics as sport governance, marketing, event management and the cultural, economic and political role of sports around the world. Students will be expected to evaluate and understand the nuances that go into global sport management and what challenges are faced by these events.
SMGT 390.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

All major theories of ethics will be examined with special application made to the sport management environment.

SMGT 320.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

SMGT 441.pre: (STAT 315 or DSCI 301) and STAT 405 and SMGT 260
SMGT 441.restr: Enrollment is limited to Undergraduate, Undergraduate Professional or Visiting Undergraduate level students.

Students will learn by writing and solving case studies as well as discussing current issues. This class is designed for students who are pursuing a career in the sport management industry. Students will also interact with a series of speakers from the industry. Students should have completed the majority of SMGT classes before considering taking this course. Repeatable for Credit.
